question:
A 23-year-old woman presents with dull lower back pain that started 4 days ago after spending an
entire day gardening. She reports occasional radiation of the pain down the back of her left leg, ending
at the posterior knee, but cannot identify specific triggers. She denies any history of chronic back pain,
and her review of systems is unremarkable. On examination, there is tenderness in the paraspinal
lumbar region, and the straight leg test is negative bilaterally. The physician diagnoses sacral somatic
dysfunction with the sacrum rotated right on a right oblique axis. Which additional finding is most likely
to be observed during the physical examination? Answer Choices: (A) Compensatory L4 rotation to the
left. (B) Positive Patrick's test on the right side. (C) Restricted sacroiliac joint mobility on the right. (D)
L5 is rotated to the right and sidebent to the left. (E) L5 is rotated to the left and sidebent to the left. (F)
Increased lumbar lordosis with forward bending. (G) A positive standing flexion test on the right. (H) A
positive seated flexion test on the left. (I) L5 is rotated to the right and sidebent to the right. (J)
Decreased sacral base movement on the right during gait.
 A. Decreased sacral base movement on the right during gait.
B. A positive standing flexion test on the right.
C. A positive seated flexion test on the left.
D. Restricted sacroiliac joint mobility on the right.
E. L5 is rotated to the left and sidebent to the left.
F. L5 is rotated to the right and sidebent to the right.
G. L5 is rotated to the right and sidebent to the left.
H. Compensatory L4 rotation to the left.
I. Increased lumbar lordosis with forward bending.
J. Positive Patrick's test on the right side.
